events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The ticket is a safety dispute: the rider's complaint alleges speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder across the whole 10.7 km RydeX trip from NUS to Raffles Place, pickup 08:36, drop-off 08:52. The trace marks the SAFE-1 screen as passed — the case is filed as a safety incident and no automatic ruling is permitted — so the only outcome available is escalation to a person [SAFE-2]. Both advocates converge on this destination (C1, D1, and both revised asks), so the ruling does not resolve the driving allegation itself.

Safety screen (read, not keyword-matched): the driver's post-trip written statement calls the rider "stupid" and accuses her of being on the phone the whole trip [F6]. That is insulting, hostile language aimed at the other party, which Ryde's code of conduct bars as abuse of any kind; I record safety_concern = "suspected" on F6 under SAFE-1. Separately, the rider's complaint of speeding, harsh braking and shoulder overtaking is a dangerous-driving allegation, which under SAFE-2 goes to a human and must not be auto-decided.

What the record actually settles: the GPS track shows the trip ran 10.6 km against a 10.7 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -1%) and took 16.1 min against a 16 min estimate (-0.4 min) [F1][F2]. This affirmatively rules out any route deviation or excess mileage under RD-1/RD-2 — there is no off-route segment fact in the file and no excess-distance charge — but it speaks only to aggregate distance and duration, not to instantaneous speed, braking, or lane use. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped, two messages: the rider's pickup note at the main entrance at 08:27 and the driver's arrival message at 08:27 [F3][F4][F5]. Read in context these are logistics, not agreement, refusal or warning, and they contain no report of unsafe driving during the trip.

What remains disputed and cannot be settled: whether the driver sped, braked hard, or used the shoulder. The file carries no telematics, speed-band or traffic fact for the actual route (get_traffic_facts returned nothing), and neither advocate disputes this; the average-duration inference from F1/F2 cannot forebear short bursts of speeding or shoulder running on a congested stretch, and it cannot corroborate them either. Under the evidence rule, missing evidence is not treated as favouring either side, and I cannot determine the driving question from the record — hence escalation, not a finding. The rider's profile (661 d, 4.6, 0 disputes in 90 d) and the driver's profile (820 d, 4.72, 455 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 d) are context only and decide nothing [F7][F8]; since no route violation is made out and neither party has a prior upheld dispute, no account flag is supported, and RD-6 does not apply.

No amount is computed: this is a fixed-fare RydeX trip charged $24.76 with no fare, ERP or add-on facts in the file, so no refundable item exists and none is claimed [F1][FARE-1]; the trace allows only escalation, and amount is null for escalate. For the reviewer: the open factual questions are (a) the driving-conduct allegation, unsupported and unrebutted by any telematics field; (b) the driver's hostile written statement [F6], which is its own SAFE-1 conduct issue; and (c) that no in-trip message records the rider warning the driver, which the reviewer should weigh against the complaint being made after the trip, without treating the silence as proof either way.

events.body:

The route itself isn't in question — 10.6 km and 16.1 minutes versus a 10.7 km, 16-minute estimate, so no detour or excess-distance issue.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint alleges dangerous driving — speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder — which is a dangerous-driving allegation; under SAFE-2 the case must go to a human and no automated ruling is issued, with the summary noting the 995 / driver commercial insurance / RydeHELP reporting routes.

The driver's written statement calls the rider 'stupid', which is an insult / personal attack in the case file; SAFE-1 requires the judge to read the words and, if found abusive, escalate rather than rule automatically and record a safety concern.

The system records show no route or time irregularity: actual distance 10.6 km vs optimal 10.7 km (-0.1 km, -1%) and duration 16.1 min vs 16 min estimated, so the rider's account cannot be corroborated or refuted by the GPS record — evidence is insufficient to apply any refund clause, which points to escalation, not to a fare remedy.

The trip is a RydeX fixed-fare trip charged $24.76 with no fare facts returned, so there is no computable overcharge and no refund under the fare clauses — the rider's remedy lies in the safety escalation, not in money.

The chat record is complete (2 messages, all timestamped) and contains only pickup logistics — the rider was at the main entrance and the driver announced arrival — with no complaint about driving raised in-trip, so the dangerous-driving allegation rests on the rider's complaint and the driver's own hostile statement, both of which the judge must read and refer to a person.

Neither party has any recorded dispute or upheld dispute in 90 days, so no flag_account request is supported on the profile evidence; the escalation should nonetheless note that the driver's statement itself is hostile toward the rider.

weaknesses: The GPS record (F1, F2) actually shows a slightly shorter and marginally faster trip than estimated (-0.1 km, -0.4 min), so the other side will argue the ride was normal and the speeding/braking claim is unverifiable — there is no telemetry field for speed or harsh braking in the fact table.

No chat message in F3/F4/F5 complains about the driving at the time, and F5 confirms the chat is complete, so the driver will say the rider never objected during the trip and raised it only afterwards.
The driver's statement (F6) insults the rider but contains no admission of speeding or shoulder-overtaking, so it supports escalation on tone, not proof of dangerous driving.
The rider's own profile (F7) shows 0 disputes in 90 days, which supports credibility but equally shows no pattern of corroborated complaints.

claims.assertion: The rider's dangerous-driving complaint (speeding, hard braking, overtaking on the shoulder) is a safety allegation, so under SAFE-2 the case must not be auto-decided; it should be escalated to a person with a factual summary, and the summary should note that the driver's own written statement is aggressive and abusive language directed at the rider ("The rider is stupid"), which is itself a SAFE-1 matter for the same human reviewer.

The only objective driving record in the file contradicts the rider's account of the trip: the GPS track shows actual distance 10.6 km against an optimal 10.7 km (-0.1 km, -1%), so there is no excess mileage of the kind that would evidence a reckless or detouring drive, and no GPS evidence of shoulder running on a longer line.

The GPS duration record also contradicts the speeding narrative: actual trip duration was 16.1 min against an estimate of 16 min (-0.4 min), i.e. the trip finished essentially on estimate, which is not consistent with sustained speeding over the whole 10.7 km route.

The fare was a fixed RydeX quote of $24.76 and no excess-distance, waiting-fee or other unbilled add-on appears in the billing record, so there is no pecuniary element for the driver to refund and no fare-based claim for the rider to recover on this safety ticket.

The rider's own conduct in the chat is consistent with a normal, cooperative pickup ('Hi, I am at the main entrance in a blue shirt.' answered by the driver's 'Arriving in 2 min, white Honda Vezel.'), and the driver sent the rider an accurate arrival message; nothing in the complete, fully timestamped chat record indicates the rider ever told the driver she felt unsafe or asked him to slow down during the trip.

The driver has 820 days on the platform, a 4.72 rating, 455 trips in 90 days and zero disputes and zero upheld disputes in the last 90 days, which is relevant context for the human reviewer on whether this isolated safety complaint warrants any account action; this profile evidence is offered only as context and does not decide the safety question.

weaknesses: My client's post-trip written statement (F6, "The rider is stupid...") is aggressive and insulting; it will be read as harassment/abuse language and triggers SAFE-1 independently of the rider's complaint, so the human reviewer will see my client as the hostile party, and it also undermines his claim that he "drove normally" by showing a hostile attitude toward the rider.

Speeding and hard braking are not recorded by any fact source in this file: I hold no telematics or speed-band record for the actual route (get_traffic_facts returned nothing, F1/F2 give only aggregate distance and duration), so I cannot affirmatively disprove harsh braking or brief speeding on segments; the rider's account (the complaint) therefore stands unrebutted on those specifics.

The rider will rely on the complaint narrative plus the gap that no in-trip chat message (F3, F4) records her warning or the driver's response, and on F6 as evidence of the driver's demeanour; the average-speed check from F1/F2 is only an inference, and a 0.4-min difference on a 16-min trip does not by itself foreclose short bursts of speeding or shoulder overtaking on a congested stretch.

points.response: Conceded in substance: I agree the case goes to a person, and as the rider's advocate I note the driver's own brief joins me in asking that the reviewer read F6, where he calls the rider 'stupid' — abusive language directed at my client that SAFE-1 requires the human reviewer to weigh alongside my client's complaint.

D2 proves nothing about driving conduct: F1 measures route length (10.6 km vs 10.7 km optimal), not speed, braking or lane use, so a driver can habitually speed and brake hard while still covering the shortest line — and RD-1 is a route-deviation clause with no bearing on a SAFE-2 dangerous-driving escalation.

F2 shows only that the whole trip averaged on estimate; it says nothing about the distribution of speed within it, and the driver's own brief concedes no telematics exist to disprove 'short bursts of speeding or shoulder overtaking on a congested stretch' — so F2 cannot rebut my client's account, it merely fails to corroborate it, which is exactly why a human must read the complaint.

I make no money claim: the trip was a fixed RydeX fare with no fare facts returned, so I ask for no refund and D4 is not in dispute — but the absence of a refundable amount does not make the safety allegation untrue, and SAFE-2 escalation is the correct outcome for a case with no pecuniary remedy.

The complete, timestamped chat (F3, F4, F5) shows only pickup logistics and nobody expects a frightened passenger to type while a driver is speeding — but the driver's own hostile statement in F6 explains the atmosphere and is the fact the reviewer should read, not the silence in F4/F5.

I do not contest F8 as context and request no flag_account against the driver; the reviewer should simply weigh F8's clean record against F6's abusive language about my client, which SAFE-1 makes a safety matter in its own right.

Conceded on the destination, contested on the effect: I never sought a fare remedy either, so escalation under SAFE-2 is common ground, but the summary should record that my client's offensive remark in his post-trip statement (F6) is itself the abusive language SAFE-1 requires the reviewer to read, so the tone problem sits on my client's side and the reviewer should treat it as a separate conduct issue from the unproven driving allegation.
